text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Human Rt on Friday laid the foundation stone of a new two billion forint ($10.6 million) plant to produce intravenous solutions.

The new plant, scheduled to be completed by the spring of 1998, will boost Human's current eight million units of annual capacity of intravenous solutions to 20 million units, said Human's project manager Andras Kubinyi.
Human said it is financing the investment from its recent capital increase and from its own sources, without tapping credit markets.

The company, majority-owned by Canada's Novopharm Ltd, the privately-held parent of Novopharm Biotech Inc, in 1996 raised its 2.8 billion forints issued share capital by one billion forints via a private placement, whose last instalment was paid in April 1997.
Prague-based Czech-Austrian Zeta-Engineering and Germany's Daldrop won tenders to deliver and instal the technology.
Board member Aron Jakabos told Reuters Human expected the investment to raise revenues from this plant to between two and three billion forints from the current one billion over the next few years.

On Friday Human shares finished at a new high of 3,610 forints, up 110, as the BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange jumped to a third successive record closing high. -- Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040 ($ = 188.2 Hungarian Forints)
